months.summary: The month saw significant developments in AI, with Anthropic's IPO valuing the company at $1.5tn, sparking concerns about an AI bubble. Anthropic also released upgraded models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, with improved capabilities and safety features. OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, with enhanced performance and lower costs. Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast and affordable AI model. Meanwhile, AI attack agents have doubled online, compromising IT systems, and state-backed hacking groups have adopted AI attack frameworks. The need for robust security measures and careful evaluation of AI capabilities has become increasingly important.

articles.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, valuing it at about $1.5tn
articles.summary: Anthropic's IPO priced at $83 a share, valuing the company at $1.5tn. This massive valuation highlights the growing hype and investment in AI, sparking concerns about an AI bubble.

articles.title: AI coding agents used firms’ own code under 60% of the time, study finds
articles.summary: Research found that AI coding agents used a company's own code in fewer than 6 out of 10 tasks, often inventing or swapping in public code instead. This highlights the limitations of relying on AI for coding tasks without proper context and oversight.

articles.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
articles.summary: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, upgraded models for technical challenges, with improved coding, reasoning, and vision capabilities, and enhanced safety features. This matters because it shows significant advancements in AI capabilities, but also highlights the need for careful evaluation and use of such powerful models.

articles.title: Anthropic Mathematician Says He Proved Riemann Hypothesis
articles.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims to have solved the Riemann Hypothesis with help from Anthropic's AI models. This matters because it would be a groundbreaking achievement in mathematics, potentially resolving a problem that has puzzled mathematicians for over 160 years.

articles.title: Introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
articles.summary: OpenAI introduces GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, with improved performance in professional outputs, coding, and computer use, at a lower cost. This matters because it could increase the reliability and trustworthiness of AI models in various applications.

articles.title: Google’s Gemini 4 Hydrogen brings a fast, cheaper model to everyone
articles.summary: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast and cheaper AI model for coding and agents, available to everyone and developers at $1.50 per million tokens. This model nearly matches Google's flagship Argon.

articles.title: Microsoft says China’s Salt Typhoon and North Korean hackers now use ARTEX
articles.summary: State-backed hacking groups from China and North Korea have added ARTEX, an AI attack framework, to their tools. This matters because it shows the increasing use of AI in cyber attacks, highlighting the need for improved security measures.

articles.title: The number of AI attack agents accessible online has almost doubled since October, Switzerland's NCSC says.
articles.source: Email: Bryson Masse from VB Daily
articles.summary: AI attack agents have doubled online since October, compromising IT systems in Switzerland. This highlights the growing threat of AI-powered attacks, which can exploit vulnerabilities and compromise systems quickly, emphasizing the need for swift security updates and robust authentication measures.

articles.title: Prompt Injection Security: Why AI Agents Need Real Controls
articles.summary: AI assistants can be vulnerable to 'prompt injection' attacks, where malicious instructions are embedded in external documents, allowing unauthorized actions to be taken. This highlights the need for robust security controls and architecture to prevent such attacks.

months.summary: The month saw significant developments in AI, with Anthropic's quarterly revenue increasing nearly 50% to $16.8bn. Google released Gemini 4 Carbon, its second major AI model in a month, and announced plans to sell its tensor processing units (TPUs) to Oracle and OpenAI. OpenAI acquired Orchestra Bio to bring AI-powered operations to life sciences R&D. Meanwhile, a study found no financial payoff from AI investments outside the tech sector, and companies are increasing cybersecurity spending due to AI-related security incidents. Researchers also proposed a method to detect covert collusion between AI agents.

articles.title: Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic's quarterly revenue increased nearly 50% to $16.8bn, with $1.70 in revenue for every $1 spent on computing power, and adjusted operating margins of 11%.

articles.title: Google to Sell AI Chips to OpenAI, Oracle
articles.summary: Google will sell its tensor processing units (TPUs) to Oracle and OpenAI, challenging Nvidia's dominance in the AI chip market.

articles.title: No Signs of AI Payoff Outside the Tech Sector
articles.summary: A study finds no financial payoff from AI investments outside the tech sector, with revenue and profit margins flat for non-tech companies. This raises concerns about the limited macroeconomic impact of AI and its potential to drive revenue growth and profit margins.

articles.title: OpenAI acquires Orchestra Bio
articles.summary: OpenAI acquires Orchestra Bio to bring AI-powered operations to life sciences R&D, accelerating drug development and advancing new treatments.

articles.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Carbon, Its Second Major AI Model in a Month
articles.summary: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, a more capable AI model than its previous one, as it tries to compete with leading AI labs. This is part of Google's efforts to improve its AI capabilities and stay competitive in the field.

articles.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
articles.summary: OpenAI will honor a shared robots.txt signal to help website operators communicate their AI training preferences to participating providers.

articles.title: ‘Nobody’s Ready’: AI-Found Bugs Spark a Corporate Security Spending Spree
articles.summary: Companies are increasing cybersecurity spending due to recent AI-related security incidents, including a hack of a root certificate authority and a vulnerability in a popular AI tool.

articles.title: S&P turns negative on Meta as AI spending eats into its cash
articles.summary: S&P lowered Meta's credit rating outlook to negative due to heavy AI spending, expecting leverage to rise above 1.0x by 2027. This highlights the financial risks of investing heavily in AI.

articles.title: Detecting Covert Collusion between AI Agents through Partner-Outsider Positive Listening
articles.summary: Researchers propose Partner-Outsider Positive Listening (PoPLi), a method to detect covert collusion between AI agents by analyzing their reactions to reworded messages. This method can help identify hidden coordination between agents.

articles.title: Scenarios for our economic future
articles.summary: Anthropic's Economics team built a model to predict the economic impact of AI on jobs, growth, and unemployment in the US by 2030, considering various scenarios of AI capabilities and usage.
